items.claim: Every Hebrew fact this row asserts over MT 15:1-15:8 holds on the bytes. items.claim: The row takes the petuchah of MT 16:35 as onset-side paragraph evidence for a row that opens at MT 16:35. On the recording convention a paragraph mark is recorded on the verse it follows, so that mark stands at the seam after MT 16:35, between MT 16:35 and MT 16:36; it is not corroboration for a seam before MT 16:35, and the extract cannot settle whether the mark instead falls inside the verse. The row covering MT 16:24-16:34 reads the very same mark in the follows-the-verse direction and discloses the one-verse discrepancy, so the two rows now give one mark opposite sides. The row's other Hebrew facts are true: the addressee-change summons stands at MT 16:35, the messenger formula at MT 16:36, MT 16:43 ends on a plain tail rather than a refrain with the utterance formula standing earlier in that verse, MT 16:43 carries exactly two variant notes with both written forms unpointed in the running text and both read forms exact substrings of that verse's own variant record, a paseq is counted at MT 16:43, and the parable label that opens the following row stands at MT 16:44, one of the book's eleven parable-label verses. The onset therefore survives on text signals alone.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 16:35 changes the addressee and issues a summons, and the messenger formula at MT 16:36 opens the judgment speech, so the text signals carry the onset without the mark. Close side: MT 16:43 ends on a plain tail, the utterance formula inside it is mid-verse, and MT 16:44 opens the sisters figure on its own parable label, so the close is argued from the forward onset. On the stated convention the paragraph mark belongs to neither of those two seams, and it must be disclosed as standing after MT 16:35 with its side unsettled by the extract.

The row's other Hebrew facts are true and its close is the best-corroborated one in the chapter's interior: the parable label stands at MT 16:44, the genealogical comparison names a Hittite mother and an Amorite father at MT 16:45 with Samaria and Sodom as the sisters at MT 16:46, MT 16:50 ends at the verse's own end with a setumah at that seam read in the correct direction, and MT 16:47 carries exactly one variant note whose read form is an exact substring of that verse's own variant record, with no other note in MT 16:44-16:50 and no paseq occurrence or editorial note in the span.
